projects.name: Alpha4Gate
projects.blurb: A StarCraft II Protoss bot that writes and validates its own code fixes to raise its win rate, streamed live on a React dashboard.
projects.card: Alpha4Gate plays StarCraft II against the game's built-in AI and its own earlier versions as a rule-based Protoss bot (with an optional PPO policy) and a Claude advisor riding shotgun, then closes the loop on itself: it drafts, tests, and validates its own code fixes to raise its own win rate. A themed two-pane self-play viewer streams two bot generations battling live; a 7-tab React dashboard shows the same game over the network. A second player, Jev, tests whether a hosted decision model can make strategic calls fast enough for a live match while its local decision graph issues every command.
proofs: Layered strategy/tactics/coherence/micro modules, each testable in isolation
Async Claude advisor -- the bot never blocks waiting on AI advice
Army coherence: staged engagement behind a critical-mass gate, strength-based retreat

relates.clause: Alpha4Gate grew out of the sc2ai_explore exploration

projects.try_it: uv run --extra viewer python scripts/selfplay.py --p1 v0 --p2 v7 --games 5

projects.name: always-best-estimates

Ledoit-Wolf is the only covariance path -- SPY/ACWI run ~0.95 correlated, a near-singular matrix otherwise
Advisory only -- binds loopback-only, never places a trade

proofs: The grader is the #1 risk -- a discrimination guard + median-over-N defend against a gameable rubric
Read-global / write-local -- reads workspace memory and project docs, writes only its own brain/ store
No vector store -- curated markdown + grep beats embeddings for a small single-author corpus

projects.name: brickomancer
projects.blurb: LEGO build suggestions from a photo or a text prompt, with 3D previews, parts lists, and a printable instruction book.
proofs: Connectivity-graph packing makes structural weakness visible before a brick is placed
Image and text inputs meet at one Shaper seam, so the 3D front-end swaps without touching the packer
Ephemeral per-request sessions -- no database, ready for a future job-history layer

projects.name: changed-check
projects.blurb: Maps a Git change set to the narrowest repository-declared validation commands, showing the full plan and rationale before running them.
proofs: Explicit mappings beat heuristics -- a check runs only because the descriptor maps a path class to it
Unknown is visible -- unmatched files produce unsupported findings, never an empty green plan
Trust boundary -- commands run as argv lists with shell=False, no shell interpolation

projects.name: citation-needed
projects.blurb: Gives each design choice in LLM-facing files a research-literature citation trail and an anchored 0-100 score, persisting vetted citations.
proofs: Zero-touch reviews -- reviewed targets gain zero bytes, output lives in a central breakdown doc
Anti-fabrication by construction -- insert_citation() is the only writer, gated by a verified fetch/API record
Two-layer split -- the CLI is deterministic and never calls an LLM itself

projects.name: coding_without_pants

proofs: Folder-as-id, derived index -- the episode list is scanned fresh every run, drift is structurally impossible
One-shot generation made dependable -- a calibrated verifier gates every generated toy before it ships
AI is an assistant, never a dependency -- every claude/whisper path degrades gracefully

One source of truth -- served and static renderers import the same model.py dataclasses
Fail-safe registry -- a malformed entry drops with a warning, never crashes the scan

Two-layer sensitive-path exclusion -- glob deny patterns plus a content-based scan guard every DB insert
Explicit roots -- every searchable root and adapter is named in config, nothing auto-crawled

projects.name: heads-up
projects.blurb: Advisory, expiring claims over repo paths/state so parallel sessions see overlapping intent before colliding, via an append-only ledger.
proofs: Advisory leases, not locks -- claims warn and provide evidence; the caller decides whether to halt
Append-only events -- active state is derived by replay, an interrupted update can't erase a claim
Append order is authoritative -- the first-appended claim wins; every later conflict is still auditable

projects.name: measure-twice
projects.blurb: A local benchmarking toolkit and mt CLI that sweeps suites across a model roster, scores them, and keeps an evidence ledger for tier claims.
proofs: Fail loud, never warn -- a tripped judge parse-gate aborts the run
Calibrate before comparing -- every scorer ships a frozen good/garbage anchor pair, CI asserts score(good) > score(garbage) forever
No judge circularity -- tier-ordering claims rest on deterministic gold answers only

relates.clause: measure-twice delegates its agreement/kill math to switchboard's calibration core

proofs: Producer/analyst separation -- reads Skill Mesh contracts, never becomes the router or writes routing decisions
Comparison requires cohorts -- incomparable records are never merged into one rate
Correlation only -- reports state sample size, missingness, and confounds

proofs: Markdown is authoritative -- the JSON index is derived and never becomes a second source of truth
Immutable history -- superseding creates a new record; existing decision meaning is never edited
Supersession fork policy -- a scalar successor; cycles and dangling targets are always illegal

proofs: One source of truth for schema + IDs -- column lists and ID formats live in modules every consumer imports

projects.name: same-page

proofs: Artifact roles are explicit -- authority is never guessed from whichever file changed most recently
Deterministic v1 -- compares normalized fields; confidence is deliberately omitted from every v1 verdict
Parse failure is not consistency -- malformed artifacts produce diagnostics, never a false-clean result

Every story project is a standalone, self-contained folder

projects.name: skill-mesh
projects.blurb: 57 provider-neutral Claude Code / GitHub Copilot skills for planning, building, reviewing, and shipping software behind a shared contract.
projects.card: skill-mesh is a provider-neutral collection of 57 agent skills spanning planning, building, reviewing, and shipping software -- each with one shared behavior contract and per-host adapters, so the same skill runs unmodified on Claude Code or GitHub Copilot. An 8-rail routing web sorts every operator fragment (a bug report, a half-formed idea, a status question) onto a pipeline rail without inventing new work; the core pipeline chains plan-init through build-phase to repo-update behind quality gates.
proofs: One shared behavior contract per skill, with per-host (Claude/Copilot) adapters
8-rail routing web sorts every operator fragment without inventing new work
Provider-neutral -- the same skill runs unmodified on Claude Code or GitHub Copilot

projects.name: switchboard

proofs: Fail-open by default -- off is byte-identical to not having switchboard wired at all
Config precedence: explicit arg -> env var -> home file -> inert defaults
The local model never owns a gate -- config only enables sites (Decision 3)

projects.name: toybox

Capability-gated -- a network outage degrades to a fully offline curated generator, no behavior change for the child

projects.name: tripwire
projects.blurb: A read-only preflight CLI that turns known workspace failure modes into fast, evidence-bearing checks over repo state and command text.
proofs: One rule owner -- checks and command explanations share IDs, severity, and provenance in one registry
Evidence before verdict -- every warn/fail carries the observed value and its source rule
Strict admission bar -- v1 contains only rules backed by a written policy or a recorded incident

projects.name: void_furnace
projects.blurb: A 'dark factory' pipeline (planner, coder, held-out critic) that turns filed GitHub issues into merged PRs on a target repo, unattended.
projects.card: void_furnace is a dark-factory autonomous coding pipeline: a planner, a coder, and a held-out critic run on a systemd timer, turning operator-filed GitHub issues into merged pull requests on a separate target repo with no human in the loop. The critic's prompt is built from the issue body, the diff, and the target's own governance docs -- structurally excluded from coder narration, so persuasive PR writing cannot buy a pass. void_furnace_calc, an arbitrary-precision Decimal calculator, is the target product it builds.
proofs: Holdout principle -- the critic never sees coder narration, PR description, or planner notes; a function signature that cannot accept them enforces it
Three-doc constitution (MISSION/FACTORY_RULES/CLAUDE.md) governs what the factory may build, precedence MISSION > FACTORY_RULES > CLAUDE
Protected-files allowlist auto-rejects PRs touching governance docs, CI config, or dependency files

relates.clause: the target product the dark factory autonomously builds

projects.name: walkies
projects.blurb: Turns live NWS weather, air quality, and estimated pavement temperature into one green/yellow/red 'can I walk my dog now?' verdict.
proofs: The verdict is the most restrictive of five independent signals -- a pleasant temperature never hides a hazardous air-quality reading
Pavement burn estimate is always paired with the 7-second back-of-hand test

projects.name: x-marks-the-spot

proofs: Seeds are the source of truth -- the DB is derived and always rebuildable from git-tracked YAML
Quarantine by schema -- scoring reads only the facts_verified view, unverified facts can't move a score
Calibration before ranking -- 11 resolved treasures are backtested; FOUND must out-band HOAX or the suite fails
